description: A slow-growing deciduous tree prized for its delicate, often deeply lobed leaves which turn vivid shades of red, orange and gold in autumn. Best in a sheltered spot away from cold winds.
A graceful native tree with distinctive white peeling bark and pendulous branches. Fast-growing and excellent for wildlife. Dappled shade beneath makes it compatible with woodland underplanting.
An early-cropping dessert apple with crisp, slightly sharp red fruit from mid-August. Attractive spring blossom important for pollinators. Self-fertile, so a single tree will produce fruit.
A robust, fast-growing evergreen shrub frequently used for dense hedging and screening. Produces spikes of white flowers in spring. Very tolerant of shade and urban conditions.

Classic aromatic sub-shrub with narrow silvery leaves and spikes of purple flowers beloved by bees and butterflies. Thrives in hot, dry positions with excellent drainage. Clip after flowering to maintain shape.
A compact evergreen shrub with glossy dark-green leaves edged with purple and long-lasting violet-blue flower spikes from summer into autumn. Good coastal and urban garden plant.

A dense, bushy evergreen shrub that earns its place in a temperate garden by flowering reliably from late autumn through spring. Flat-topped pink and white flower clusters are followed by metallic blue berries.

Classic deciduous shrub with large round flower heads in blue or pink depending on soil pH. Blue tones occur in acidic soil; pink in alkaline. Flowers last from midsummer into autumn and dry attractively.
Aromatic evergreen shrub with needle-like silvery-green leaves and small blue-purple flowers in spring and early summer. Attractive to bees. Thrives in poor, dry soil in a sunny position.
Rounded evergreen shrub with aromatic, glossy three-lobed leaves and clusters of sweetly fragrant white flowers in spring and often again in autumn. Very adaptable and reliable in milder gardens.
AGM-winning hardy perennial with a very long flowering season from early summer through to the first frosts. Violet-blue flowers with a white eye spread over a mounding ground-covering form.
Upright perennial with large, daisy-like flowers with drooping pink-purple ray florets surrounding a prominent orange-brown central cone. Attracts bees, butterflies and goldfinches in autumn.

Evergreen perennial grown primarily for its dramatic, deeply lobed leaves of deep metallic purple-bronze. Small white flowers rise on wiry stems in summer. Useful for year-round colour in shaded spots.
verification_note: RHS pages for this plant carry no growing data. Verified against Missouri Botanical Garden Plant Finder (feet converted to metres). RHS hardiness rating is NOT verified.

description: Upright perennial with deep violet-blue flower spikes on black stems from early summer. Deadhead or cut back after the first flush to encourage a second wave of bloom. Excellent front-of-border plant.

Tough, spreading perennial with flat-topped flower heads in white, pink or yellow, held above feathery aromatic foliage. Drought-tolerant once established, excellent for wildlife. Spreads readily to form colonies.

Classic cottage garden perennial with scalloped, water-repelling leaves and frothy sprays of lime-yellow-green flowers in early summer. Remarkably adaptable and self-seeds freely. Excellent for path edging.
Cottage garden stalwart with intricate, pin-cushion flower heads in white, pink or deep red, surrounded by papery star-shaped bracts. Flowers from early summer. Tolerates damp conditions well.

Award-winning hosta with slug-resistant, heart-shaped leaves of steely blue-grey. Lavender-blue tubular flowers in summer. One of the most reliable hostas for providing bold, structural foliage in shade.

Stately biennial or short-lived perennial producing tall spires of tubular purple (or white) spotted flowers beloved by bumblebees. Self-seeds freely to naturalise in informal settings. All parts toxic if ingested.

Reliable perennial with tubular, wine-red flowers with a white-striped throat produced in great abundance from early summer until the first frosts. Semi-evergreen in mild winters. Best left unpruned until spring.
verification_note: RHS lists this plant as semi-evergreen.

description: Fine-textured clump-forming grass with hair-like, pale green leaves that turn golden-blond by late summer. Moves beautifully in the slightest breeze. Can self-seed invasively in warm climates.
Tall, elegant clump-forming grass with narrow arching leaves that have a white midrib. Reddish-copper plumes appear in autumn and persist through winter, providing structure and seed for birds.
Bold, architectural sedge with broad arching evergreen leaves and long, drooping dark-brown catkin-like flower spikes. Tolerates wet and deeply shaded conditions where few other plants thrive.

Vigorous self-clinging evergreen climber or ground-cover. Invaluable for covering walls, fences or bare ground in shade. Autumn nectar and winter berries are important for wildlife. Can damage weak mortar if unchecked.

Classic large-flowered clematis with deep purple-blue flowers 15-18 cm across from early summer. Best with its roots in shade and top growth in sun. Prune to 30 cm in early spring for the best flowers.

Award-winning English rose with deep pink, deeply cupped blooms and an outstanding classic rose fragrance. Repeat-flowers well through summer. One of the most reliable David Austin roses for UK and Irish gardens.
Vigorous, mat-forming evergreen ground cover with small, glossy dark-green leaves and periwinkle-blue flowers from early spring. Excellent for suppressing weeds under trees or on shady banks.

Tough, spreading evergreen with dark rosettes of leathery leaves and bright yellow-green flower heads in spring. One of the best plants for dry shade under trees. Spreads via underground stolons to form weed-suppressing colonies.

AGM-winning dwarf daffodil producing multiple cheerful golden-yellow flowers per stem in early to mid-spring. Perfectly scaled for borders, containers, or naturalising in grass. Very reliable and long-lived.

Striking ornamental onion producing perfectly spherical heads of deep violet-purple flowers in late spring to early summer. Plant in drifts among perennials for a striking vertical accent. Attractive to bees.
Robust, shuttlecock-forming deciduous fern producing fresh green fronds in spring. Very tolerant of deep shade and challenging soils. One of the most adaptable British native ferns for garden use.

Bold architectural plant with strap-like, sword-shaped evergreen leaves in bronze, green or variegated forms. Provides strong structural interest year-round. Best in a sheltered coastal or mild urban garden.

Free-flowering sub-shrub with narrow grey-green leaves and dense spikes of mauve flowers produced almost continuously from early spring into summer. Needs replacing every 2-3 years as it becomes woody and exhausted.

Tall, airy perennial with square stems that branch at the top to carry clusters of bright purple flowers from midsummer to autumn. Its see-through habit means it can be planted at the front or middle of a border without blocking views.

Reliable, clump-forming perennial with golden-yellow ray florets surrounding a dark brown central cone. Flowers from late summer until the first frosts. AGM winner and exceptionally reliable in temperate gardens.

Vigorous, clump-forming perennial with slender, bright crimson flower spikes produced from midsummer until autumn. Very adaptable and low-maintenance. Provides reliable late-season colour and structure.
Hardy agapanthus producing large, drumstick-like heads of violet-blue or white trumpet flowers on tall stems in midsummer. The hardiest strain of agapanthus; thrives in a sunny well-drained border.

Upright, architectural grass with stiff stems topped by feathery pinkish-purple plumes that fade to wheat-gold. One of the first ornamental grasses to come into growth in spring. Holds its form well into winter.
Compact moor grass with upright flower stems that dance in the wind. Foliage turns bright yellow in autumn before falling cleanly away. Performs well in acidic or boggy soils.

Vigorous twining climber with intensely fragrant, creamy-white and purple-red flowers from midsummer to autumn. Red berries follow, popular with birds. The late-season cultivar extends the display well into autumn.

Spectacular deciduous climber with drooping racemes of fragrant lilac-blue flowers before the leaves emerge in spring. Requires a sturdy support and a programme of twice-yearly pruning to flower well.

Spreading, low-growing evergreen subshrub with whorled, glossy leaves and small white flower spikes in spring. One of the most reliable ground-cover plants for dense shade under trees. Slow to establish but long-lasting.

Hardy, easy evergreen with rosettes of rounded, slightly fleshy leaves and airy sprays of tiny pink-spotted white flowers in late spring. Very adaptable and tolerant of difficult conditions including dry shade.

Single late tulip with deep maroon-black goblet-shaped flowers that look almost velvety. One of the most dramatic tulip cultivars, effective in bold drifts or in containers. Lift and store bulbs after flowering.

Britain's most loved wildflower, with nodding one-sided sprays of fragrant violet-blue bells in late spring. Naturalises freely under deciduous trees and shrubs to create sweeping drifts. Do not confuse with the Spanish bluebell.
One of the first flowers of the year, producing bright yellow cup-shaped blooms on bare stems in January and February, backed by a ruff of leaf-like bracts. Naturalises freely under deciduous trees.

Spreading deciduous shrub or small tree producing spidery, copper-orange flowers with a soft fragrance on bare branches in midwinter. Leaves turn brilliant orange-red in autumn. Requires acid to neutral soil.

Upright evergreen shrub with bold architectural pinnate leaves and long, spreading racemes of fragrant yellow flowers from late autumn through winter. Excellent for shaded spots where winter colour is needed.

Classic native evergreen tree or large shrub with glossy, spiny leaves and bright red berries in autumn and winter. Essential wildlife plant: berries feed birds, thorny foliage provides safe nesting. Grows well in shade.

Deciduous shrub grown primarily for its brilliant crimson winter stems, which are most vivid when cut back hard each spring. White flowers in summer, autumn colour and white berries add further interest through the year.

Tough, free-flowering deciduous shrub with pendulous red and purple flowers beloved by hummingbirds in its native range and by bees and butterflies here. Particularly well-suited to mild, western gardens in the UK and Ireland.
verification_note: RHS lists this plant as deciduous or semi-evergreen.

description: Handsome evergreen shrub with oval, wavy-edged leaves of pale grey-green margined with creamy-white. Very popular in coastal and urban gardens in mild areas. Provides year-round foliage interest.

Compact evergreen shrub producing tiny but intensely fragrant white flowers on bare stems in midwinter, followed by shiny black berries. One of the best plants for a shaded spot where fragrance is needed in the dullest months.

Vigorous evergreen shrub bearing exceptionally long, grey-green catkins from midwinter into spring. Best grown against a sheltered wall in colder areas. Its winter display is unmatched for structure in the garden.

Elegant, slow-growing evergreen with small, dark green toothed leaves and clusters of intensely fragrant, small white tubular flowers in spring. Easily clipped into a formal shape or allowed to grow as an informal mound.

Strikingly architectural evergreen with blue-grey leaves and enormous yellow-green flower heads from early spring until early summer. Spectacular in mass plantings. Milky sap is a severe skin irritant.

Clump-forming perennial with slender, upright grass-like leaves and elegant blue-violet flowers in early summer. Very easy and long-lived. Good at the margins of a pond or boggy ground, also tolerates ordinary borders.

Classic cottage garden peony with large, fully double, pale rose-pink flowers in late spring to early summer with a sweet fragrance. Long-lived once established, resenting disturbance. Plant with the buds no deeper than 5 cm.

Prickly, metallic-blue thistle-like perennial with rigid, branching stems. Flowers and bracts develop an intense steel-blue colour in summer. Thrives in poor, dry soil in full sun. Excellent for cutting and drying.

Dramatic perennial with strap-like grey-green leaves and striking torches of tubular flowers grading from red-orange at the top to yellow at the base. Loved by bumblebees and hummingbirds. Requires excellent drainage.
Hardy, fragrant purple flower spikes in summer; needs well-drained soil to survive wet winters.
Deep purple foliage turning bright red in autumn; prefers shelter from strong coastal winds.
Large lime-white summer flower cones; extremely hardy and handles heavy rain well.
Glossy green foliage with bright red young growth; widely sold for evergreen screening and hedging.
Repeat-flowering English rose with strong disease resistance and fragrance; thrives in UK and Irish clay soils.
Bi-coloured red and white blooms from summer into late autumn; drought-tolerant and pollinator-friendly.
Vigorous summer-flowering climber with large velvety purple flowers; prefers shaded roots and sunny tops.
Glossy evergreen leaves and scented white summer flowers; best against a warm, sheltered wall.
Glossy dark foliage with rose-like blooms in late winter/spring; requires ericaceous (acidic) soil.
Self-clinging climber with white lacecap flowers; ideal for north-facing walls in Britain and Ireland.
Bright golden-yellow evergreen foliage that brightens shady borders year-round.
Deep red winter flower buds opening to scented white spring blooms; compact and shade-loving.
Brilliant red young spring foliage fading to cream and green; needs acidic, moisture-retentive soil.
Hardy, reliable white-flowered evergreen shrub suited to acidic soils and high-rainfall areas.
Purple-tinged foliage and violet summer flower spikes; thrives in mild coastal UK and Irish gardens.
Tough, low-growing variegated groundcover or container shrub; handles pollution and shade easily.
Upright, narrow evergreen frequently sold as a blight-free alternative to box hedging.
Traditional clipping shrub for formal parterres and topiary; thrives in chalky or clay soils.
Native, long-lived evergreen for formal hedges and topiary; tolerates heavy pruning and deep shade.
Dark glossy leaves on reddish stems; a refined, hardy hedging choice across Britain and Ireland.
Apple-green leathery leaves; arguably the most popular salt-tolerant coastal hedging plant in Ireland and western UK.
Glossy leaves and tubular pink summer flowers; excels in seaside and windy maritime gardens.
Silvery-green leaves and intensely scented autumn flowers; impervious to coastal salt winds.
Bright yellow flowers on bare green stems from November to March; completely hardy.
Fragrant yellow ribbon-like flowers on bare branches in mid-winter; vibrant autumn leaf colour.
Reliable burst of golden-yellow flowers in early spring; tough and easy to grow in any soil.
Clusters of deep pink spring blooms; hardy, fast-growing, and tolerant of poor soils.
Classic scented purple or white flower panicles in late spring; very hardy and alkaline-tolerant.
Arching branches covered in orange-blossom scented white flowers in early summer.
Cream-edged leaves and clusters of soft pink tubular flowers in late spring and early summer.
Bronze-gold spring foliage turning green with flat pink summer flower heads; compact and low-maintenance.
Long-flowering compact shrub with pure white blooms from late spring to autumn; thrives in poor soil.
Deep purple scented flower spikes in mid-to-late summer; prolific pollinator magnet.
Covered in vivid cobalt-blue flowers in late spring; best against a sheltered, sunny wall.
Thorny wall shrub prized for white spring blossom and dense clusters of orange berries loved by birds.
Variegated silvery-grey and white foliage; invaluable for shady walls, hanging baskets, and groundcover.
Native-type climbing honeysuckle with sweet-scented creamy-yellow flowers from mid-summer to autumn.
Exotic white-and-purple flowers followed by orange fruits; hardy against sheltered south- or west-facing walls.
Repeat-flowering pearl-pink climbing rose with glossy, disease-resistant leaves; tolerates partial shade.
Compact native tree with spring blossom, bright red late-summer berries, and fiery autumn leaves.
White-and-pink spring blossom followed by persistent orange-red fruits; great pollinator for garden apples.
Iconic double-pink spring blossom clusters; hardy and widely planted in British and Irish gardens.
Starry white spring flowers, bronze young leaves, and rich orange-red autumn foliage; thrives in damp soils.
Sold widely as a patio specimen; hardy in sheltered UK/Irish gardens if given sharp winter drainage.
Palm-like spiky foliage widely grown across Ireland and coastal Britain; thrives in mild maritime air.
Bold sword-shaped bronze-purple leaves; wind-resistant and ideal for coastal or contemporary borders.
Large glossy palmate leaves giving a tropical look while being fully hardy in shaded borders.
Nodding winter-to-spring blooms in white, pink, and plum; thrives under deciduous trees and shrubs.
verification_note: RHS lists this plant as semi-evergreen

description: Delicate white nodding flowers emerging in January and February; naturalises well in damp grass or woodland.
Silvery-lilac cup flowers in February; early pollen source for emerging bumblebees.
Towering summer spires in true blues, purples, and whites; needs staking and slug protection in spring.
Bold, colourful early-summer flower spikes; thrives in cool UK/Irish summers and slightly acidic soils.
Huge papery blooms in scarlet, salmon, or white in early summer; bold cottage-garden favourite.
Delicate spurred flowers in late spring; self-seeds gently into shady or sunny cottage borders.
Arching stems hung with heart-shaped pink-and-white flowers in late spring; loves cool, moist shade.
Feathery plumes of crimson flowers above fern-like leaves; thrives in damp soils and beside ponds.
Aromatic grey-green foliage and clouds of lavender-blue blooms from May to September; tough and drought-proof.
Silvery stems and airy violet-blue flower spikes in late summer; thrives in free-draining, sunny spots.
Essential late-autumn colour in purples, pinks, and blues when most perennials are fading.
Tall, graceful white flowers with yellow centres from August to October; thrives in damp, shaded borders.
verification_note: RHS lists this plant as deciduous or semi-evergreen

description: Succulent grey-green leaves and flat pink flowerheads turning coppery-red in autumn; great for bees.
Sterile hybrid producing non-stop apricot-orange flowers from May to September; slug-resistant.
Intricate pincushion-like pink flowers from early to late summer; thrives in moist, humus-rich soil.
Heart-shaped silver-veined leaves and sprays of tiny blue forget-me-not flowers in spring.
White-spotted leaves and early spring flowers; early nectar source that thrives in cool, damp shade.
Tough leathery leaves turning red in winter, with pink spring flower clusters; thrives in poor or damp soil.

description: Sword-like leaves and arching sprays of fiery red summer blooms; thrives in damp maritime climates.
Architectural torch-like spikes of warm orange and cream blooms in summer; loves coastal and sunny sites.
Low-growing mats of tiny white-and-pink daisies from May to November; ideal for wall crevices and gravel.
verification_note: RHS lists this plant as semi-evergreen

description: Glossy, strap-like evergreen fronds native to Britain and Ireland; thrives in damp shade and alkaline soils.
